1.1: In the first year of plenty, in the second month, on the fifth of the month, Pharaoh sent Yosĕph to go around all the land of Mitsrayim; and in the fourth month of the first year, on the eighteenth of the month, Yosĕph came to the borders of On, and he was gathering the grain of that country like the sand of the sea.
1.2: And there was a certain man in that city named Poti-Phera, who was a priest of On and a satrap of Pharaoh, and chief of all Pharaoh’s satraps and princes; and this man was exceedingly rich and very wise and gentle, and he was also a counselor of Pharaoh, because he was prudent beyond all Pharaoh’s princes.
1.3: And he had a virgin daughter named Asenath, eighteen years old, tall and graceful, and exceedingly beautiful to look at, beyond every virgin on the earth.
1.4: Now Asenath herself bore no likeness to the virgins, the daughters of the Mitsrites, but was in all things like the daughters of the Iḇrim, being tall like Sarah, graceful like Riḇqah, and beautiful like Raḥĕl; and the fame of her beauty spread abroad through all that land and to the ends of the world, so that because of this all the sons of the princes and the satraps desired to woo her, yes, and the sons of the melaḵim also, all young and mighty men; and there was great strife among them because of her, and they tried to fight against one another.
1.5: And Pharaoh’s first-born son also heard about her, and he kept pleading with his father to give her to him as a wife, saying to him: "Give me, father, Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Phera, the first man of On, as my wife."
1.6: And his father Pharaoh said to him: "Why do you, for your part, seek a wife lower than yourself, when you are meleḵ of all this land? No, but see, the daughter of Joaqim the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ is betrothed to you, and she herself is a queen and exceedingly beautiful to look at. Take this one, then, to be your wife."

10.1: And when Yosĕph had left the house, Poti-Phera also and all his relatives departed to their inheritance, and Asenath was left alone with the seven virgins, listless and weeping until the sun set; and she neither ate bread nor drank water, but while all slept she alone was awake, weeping and often beating her breast with her hand.
10.2: And after these things Asenath rose from her bed, and went quietly down the stairs from the loft, and on coming to the gateway found the gatekeeper sleeping with her children; and she hurried and took down from the door the leather cover of the curtain and filled it with cinders and carried it up to the loft and laid it on the floor.
10.3: And then she shut the door securely and fastened it with the iron bolt from the side and groaned with great groaning, together with much and very great weeping.
10.4: But the virgin whom Asenath loved above all the virgins, having heard her groaning, hurried and came to the door after waking the other virgins also, and found it shut.
10.5: And when she had listened to the groaning and the weeping of Asenath, she said to her, standing outside: "What is it, my mistress, and why are you sad? And what is it that troubles you? Open to us and let us see you."
10.6: And Asenath said to her, being shut inside: "Great and grievous pain has attacked my head, and I am resting in my bed, and I am not able to rise and open to you, for I am weak in all my limbs. So go, each of you, to her chamber and sleep, and let me be still."
10.7: And when the virgins had departed, each to her own chamber, Asenath rose and opened the door of her bedroom quietly, and went away into her second chamber where the chests of her adornment were, and she opened her chest and took a black and somber tunic which she had put on and mourned in when her first-born brother died.
10.8: Having taken this tunic, then, she carried it into her chamber, and again shut the door securely, and put the bolt in place from the side.
10.9: Then Asenath took off her royal robe and put on the mourning tunic, and loosed her golden girdle and girded herself with a rope, and took off the tiara, that is, the miter, from her head, and likewise the diadem, and the chains from her hands and her feet were also all laid on the floor.
10.10: Then she takes her choice robe and the golden girdle and the miter and her diadem, and she threw them through the window that looked toward the north, to the poor.
10.11: And then she took all her elohim that were in her chamber, the elohim of gold and of silver of which there was no number, and broke them into fragments, and threw them through the window to poor men and beggars.
10.12: And again Asenath took her royal dinner, and the fatlings and the fish and the heifer’s flesh, and all the sacrifices of her elohim, and the vessels of the wine of libation, and threw them all through the window that looked north as food for the dogs.
10.13: And after these things she took the leather cover containing the cinders and poured them on the floor; and then she took sackcloth and girded her loins; and she also loosed the net of the hair of her head and sprinkled ashes over her head.
10.14: And she also strewed cinders on the floor, and fell upon the cinders and kept beating her breast constantly with her hands and weeping all the night with groaning until the morning.
10.15: And when Asenath arose in the morning and looked, see, the cinders beneath her were like clay from her tears; and she again fell on her face upon the cinders until the sun set.
10.16: Thus Asenath did for seven days, tasting nothing at all.

11.1: And on the eighth day, when the dawn came and the birds were already chirping and the dogs barking at the passers-by, Asenath lifted up her head a little from the floor and the cinders on which she was seated, because she was exceedingly weary and had lost the power of her limbs from her great humiliation; for Asenath had grown weary and faint and her strength was failing, and then she turned toward the wall, sitting under the window that looked east; and she laid her head on her bosom, twining the fingers of her hands over her right knee; and her mouth was shut, and she did not open it during the seven days and during the seven nights of her humiliation.
11.2: And she said in her heart, not opening her mouth: "What shall I do, I the lowly one, or where shall I go?
11.3: And with whom again shall I find refuge from now on?
11.4: Or to whom shall I speak, the virgin who is an orphan and desolate and abandoned by all and hated?
11.5: All have now come to hate me, and among them even my father and my mother, because I spurned the elohim with loathing and did away with them and have given them to the poor to be destroyed by men.
11.6: For my father and my mother said: 'Asenath is not our daughter.'
11.7: But all my relatives also have come to hate me, and all men, because I have given their elohim to destruction.
11.8: And I have hated every man and all who wooed me, and now in this humiliation of mine I have been hated by all, and they rejoice over my tribulation.
11.9: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of the mighty Yosĕph, hates all who worship the idols, because He is a jealous Elohim and terrible, as I have heard, against all who worship strange elohim; therefore He has hated me also, because I worshipped dead and deaf idols and baraḵ them.
11.10: But now I have shunned their sacrifice, and my mouth has become estranged from their table, and I have no courage to call on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of the shamayim, the Most High and powerful one of the mighty Yosĕph, because my mouth is polluted from the sacrifices of the idols.
11.11: But I have heard many saying that the Elohim of the Iḇrim is a true Elohim, and a living Elohim, and a merciful Elohim, and compassionate and long-suffering and full of mercy and gentle, and one who does not count the sin of a man who is humble, and especially of one who sins in ignorance, and does not convict of lawless deeds in the time of the affliction of a man who is afflicted; so I also, the humble one, will be bold and will turn to Him and seek refuge with Him and confess all my sins to Him and pour out my petition before Him, and He will have mercy on my misery.
11.12: For who knows if He will see this humiliation of mine and the desolation of my soul and pity me, and will see also the orphanhood of my wretchedness and virginity and defend me?
11.13: For, as I hear, He is Himself a father of orphans and a consolation of the afflicted and a helper of the persecuted.
11.14: But in any case I also, the humble one, will be bold and will cry to Him."
11.15: Then Asenath rose up from the wall where she was sitting, and raised herself on her knees toward the east and directed her eyes toward the shamayim and opened her mouth and said to Elohim:

12.1: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of the righteous, who created the ages and gives life to all things, who gave the breath of life to all Your creation, who brought the invisible things out into the light, who made all things and made manifest things that did not appear, who lifted up the shamayim and founded the earth on the waters, who fixed the great stones on the abyss of the water, which shall not be submerged but are doing Your will to the end, because You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, spoke the word and all things came into being, and Your word, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, is the life of all Your creatures; to You I flee for refuge, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, from now on; to You I will cry, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and to You I will confess my sins, to You I will pour out my petition, Master, and to You I will reveal my lawless deeds.
12.2: Spare me, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, spare me, because I committed many sins against You; I did lawlessness and wickedness, I have spoken things not to be uttered, and wicked in Your sight; my mouth, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, has been polluted from the sacrifices of the idols of the Mitsrites, and from the table of their elohim: I sinned, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I sinned in Your sight, both in knowledge and in ignorance I did wickedness in that I worshipped dead and deaf idols, and I am not worthy to open my mouth to You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I the miserable Asenath, daughter of Poti-Phera the priest, the virgin and queen, who was once proud and haughty and one who prospered in my father’s riches above all men, but now an orphan and desolate and abandoned by all men.
12.3: To You I flee, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and to You I offer my petition, and to You I will cry.
12.4: Deliver me from those who pursue me, Master, before I am taken by them; for, as an infant in fear of someone flees to his father and mother, and his father stretches out his hands and catches him up against his breast, so also You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, stretch out Your undefiled and terrible hands on me like a child-loving father, and catch me out of the hand of the unseen enemy.
12.5: For see, the ancient and savage and cruel lion pursues me, because he is the father of the elohim of the Mitsrites, and the elohim of the idol-crazed are his children, and I have come to hate them, and I did away with them, because they are a lion’s children, and I cast all the elohim of the Mitsrites from me and did away with them, and the lion, their father the devil, in wrath against me is trying to swallow me up.
12.6: But You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, deliver me from his hands, and I shall be rescued from his mouth, lest he tear me apart and cast me into the flame of fire, and the fire cast me into storm, and the storm prevail over me in darkness and cast me into the depth of the sea, and the great beast who is from everlasting swallow me up, and I perish forever.
12.7: Deliver me, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, before all these things come upon me; deliver me, Master, the desolate and defenseless, because my father and my mother have denied me and said, 'Asenath is not our daughter,' because I broke their elohim in pieces and did away with them, as having wholly hated them.
12.8: And now I am an orphan and desolate, and I have no other hope except You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, nor another refuge except Your mercy, O friend of men, because You alone are the father of the orphans and champion of the persecuted and helper of the afflicted.
12.9: Have mercy on me, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and keep me pure and virgin, the forsaken one and orphan, because You alone, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are a sweet and good and gentle father.
12.10: For what father is sweet and good as You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
12.11: For see, all the houses of my father Poti-Phera which he has given me for an inheritance are for a time and vanishing; but the houses of Your inheritance, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are incorruptible and eternal."

13.1: "Look upon my humiliation, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and have mercy on my orphanhood and pity me, the afflicted.
13.2: For see, I, Master, fled from all and sought refuge with You, the only friend of men.
13.3: See, I left all the good things of the earth and sought refuge with You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, in sackcloth and ashes, naked and solitary.
13.4: See, now I have put off my royal robe of fine linen and of crimson cloth interwoven with gold and have put on a black tunic of mourning.
13.5: See, I have loosed my golden girdle and cast it from me and girded myself with rope and sackcloth.
13.6: See, I have cast my diadem and my miter from my head, and I have sprinkled myself with cinders.
13.7: See, the floor of my chamber that was paved with stones of many colors and of purple, which was formerly moistened with ointments and was dried with bright linen cloths, is now moistened with my tears and has been dishonored in that it is strewn with ashes.
13.8: See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the cinders and my tears much clay has been formed in my chamber as on a broad road.
13.9: See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I have given my royal dinner and the meats to the dogs.
13.10: See, I have also, Master, been fasting seven days and seven nights and have neither eaten bread nor drunk water, and my mouth is dry as a wheel and my tongue as horn and my lips as a potsherd, and my face has shrunk, and my eyes have failed from shedding tears.
13.11: But You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, deliver me from my many acts of ignorance, and forgive me because, being a virgin and unknowing, I have gone astray.
13.12: See, now all the elohim whom I worshipped before in ignorance I have now come to know to have been deaf and dead idols, and I broke them in pieces and gave them to be trampled on by all men, and the thieves plundered them, for they were gold and silver; and with You I sought refuge, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, the only compassionate one and friend of men.
13.13: Forgive me, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, because I committed many sins against You in ignorance and have spoken blasphemous words against my master Yosĕph, and I, the miserable one, did not know that he is Your son, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, since the wicked men urged by envy said to me: 'Yosĕph is the son of a shepherd from the land of Kena’an,' and I, the miserable one, believed them and went astray, and I despised him and have spoken wicked things about him, not knowing that he is Your son.
13.14: For who among men has fathered or will ever father such beauty? Or who else is like him, wise and mighty like the all-beautiful Yosĕph?
13.15: But to You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I entrust him, because for my part I love him more than my soul.
13.16: Keep him safe in the wisdom of Your favor, and entrust me to him as a female servant and a slave, that I may wash his feet and make his bed and minister to him and serve him, and I will be a slave to him for the times of my life."

14.1: And when Asenath had ceased making confession to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, see, the morning star also rose out of the shamayim in the east; and Asenath saw it and rejoiced and said: "Has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim then heard my prayer? For this star is a messenger and herald of the light of the great day."
14.2: And see, close by the morning star the shamayim was torn open and a great and ineffable light appeared.
14.3: And when she saw it, Asenath fell on her face on the cinders, and immediately there came to her a man from the shamayim, sending forth rays of light, and stood above her head.
14.4: And as she lay on her face, the divine messenger said to her, "Asenath, stand up."
14.5: And she said: "Who is he that called me? For the door of my chamber is shut and the tower is high; how then has he come into my chamber?"
14.6: And he called her again a second time, saying, "Asenath, Asenath."
14.7: And she said, "Here I am, master; tell me who you are."
14.8: And he said: "I am the chief commander of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim and commander of all the host of the Most High; stand up and stand on your feet, that I may speak my words to you."
14.9: And she lifted up her face and looked, and see, a man in all things like Yosĕph, in robe and wreath and royal staff, except that his face was like lightning, and his eyes like the light of the sun, and the hairs of his head like the flame of fire of a burning torch, and his hands and his feet like iron shining from fire, for sparks, as it were, proceeded both from his hands and from his feet.
14.10: Seeing these things, Asenath was afraid and fell on her face, unable even to stand on her feet, for she became greatly afraid and all her limbs trembled.
14.11: And the man said to her: "Take courage, Asenath, and do not fear; but stand up and stand on your feet, that I may speak my words to you."
14.12: Then Asenath stood up and stood on her feet, and the messenger said to her: "Go without hindrance into your second chamber and lay aside the black tunic in which you are clothed, and cast off the sackcloth from your loins, and shake out the cinders from your head, and wash your face and your hands with pure water, and put on a white untouched robe and gird your loins with the bright girdle of virginity, the double one, and come again to me, and I will speak to you the words that are sent to you from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄."
14.13: Then Asenath hurried and went into her second chamber, where the chests of her adornment were, and opened her chest and took a white, fine, untouched robe and put it on, having first put off the black robe, and she also ungirded the rope and the sackcloth from her loins and girded herself with a bright, double girdle of her virginity, one girdle about her loins and another girdle about her breast.
14.14: And she also shook out the cinders from her head and washed her hands and face with pure water, and she took a most beautiful and fine mantle and veiled her head.

15.1: And then she came to the divine chief commander and stood before him, and the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 says to her: "Take the mantle from your head now, for today you are a pure virgin, and your head is like that of a young man."
15.2: And Asenath took it from her head.
15.3: And again the divine messenger says to her: "Take courage, Asenath, the virgin and pure, for see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim heard all the words of your confession and your prayer, and He has also seen the humiliation and affliction of the seven days of your abstinence, for from your tears much clay has been formed before your face on these cinders.
15.4: So take courage, Asenath, the virgin and pure, for see, your name has been written in the book of life and shall never be blotted out; but from this day you shall be renewed and refashioned and made alive again, and you shall eat the baruḵ bread of life and drink a cup filled with immortality and be anointed with the baruḵ ointment of incorruption.
15.5: Take courage, Asenath, the virgin and pure; see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim has given you today to Yosĕph as a bride, and he himself shall be your bridegroom forever.
15.6: And no longer shall you be called Asenath, but your name shall be 'City of Refuge,' for in you many nations shall seek refuge and they shall lodge under your wings, and many nations shall find shelter through you, and on your walls those who cling to Elohim Most High through penitence shall be kept secure; for Penitence is the daughter of the Most High, and she herself entreats Elohim Most High for you every hour and for all who repent, since He is the father of Penitence, and she herself is the completion and overseer of all virgins, loving you exceedingly and beseeching the Most High for you every hour, and for all who repent she will provide a place of rest in the shamayim, and she renews everyone who has repented.
15.7: And Penitence is exceedingly beautiful, a virgin pure and gentle and mild; and therefore Elohim Most High loves her, and all the messengers revere her, and I love her exceedingly, for she herself is also my sister, and as she loves you virgins, I also love you.
15.8: And see, for my part I am going to Yosĕph and will speak to him all these words concerning you, and he will come to you today and see you and rejoice over you and love you and be your bridegroom, and you shall be his beloved bride forever.
15.9: So hear me, Asenath, and put on a wedding robe, the ancient and first robe that is still laid up in your chamber from of old, and put all your choice adornment about you as well, and adorn yourself as a good bride and make yourself ready to meet him; for see, he himself is coming to you today and will see you and rejoice."
15.10: And when the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the shape of a man had finished speaking these words to Asenath, she rejoiced with great joy over all the things that were spoken by him, and fell on her face on the earth, and bowed down before his feet and said to him: "Baruḵ is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim who sent you to deliver me from the darkness and to bring me from the foundations of the abyss itself into the light, and baruḵ is your name forever.
15.11: If then I have found favor, my master, in your sight, and shall know that you will perform all the words which you have said to me so that they are accomplished, let your female servant speak to you."
15.12: And the messenger says to her, "Speak."
15.13: And she said: "Please, master, sit down a little while on this bed, because this bed is pure and undefiled, for no other man or other woman ever sat on it, and I will set before you a table and bread, and you shall eat, and I will also bring you wine, old and good, whose fragrance shall reach to the shamayim, and you shall drink of it and afterward depart on your way."
15.14: And he says to her: "Hurry and bring it quickly."

16.1: And Asenath hurried and set an empty table before him; and as she was starting to fetch bread, the divine messenger says to her: "Bring me also a honeycomb."
16.2: And she stood still and was perplexed and grieved, because she did not have a bee’s comb in her storehouse.
16.3: And the divine messenger says to her: "Why are you standing still?"
16.4: And she said: "My master, I will send a boy to the suburb, because the possession of our inheritance is near, and he will come and bring one quickly from there, and I will set it before you."
16.5: The divine messenger says to her: "Enter your storehouse and you will find a bee’s comb lying on the table; take it up and bring it here."
16.6: And she said, "Master, there is no bee’s comb in my storehouse."
16.7: And he said, "Go, and you will find."
16.8: And Asenath entered her storehouse and found a honeycomb lying on the table; and the comb was great and white like snow and full of honey, and that honey was like the dew of the shamayim, and its fragrance like the fragrance of life.
16.9: Then Asenath wondered and said within herself: "Is this comb from the mouth of this man himself?"
16.10: And Asenath took that comb and brought it and set it out on the table, and the messenger said to her: "Why is it that you said, 'There is no honeycomb in my house,' and see, you have brought it to me?"
16.11: And she said: "Master, I have never put a honeycomb in my house, but as you said, so it has been made. Did this come forth from your mouth? For its fragrance is like the fragrance of ointment."
16.12: And the man smiled at the woman’s understanding.
16.13: Then he calls her to himself, and when she came, he stretched out his right hand and took hold of her head, and when he shook her head with his right hand, Asenath feared the messenger’s hand greatly, because sparks proceeded from his hands in the manner of red-hot iron, and so she was all the time gazing with much fear and trembling at the messenger’s hand.
16.14: And he smiled and said: "Baruḵ are you, Asenath, because the ineffable mysteries of Elohim have been revealed to you; and baruḵ are all who cling to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim in penitence, because they shall eat of this comb, for this comb is the spirit of life, and the bees of the Paradise of delight have made it from the dew of the roses of life that are in the Paradise of Elohim and every flower, and the messengers and all the elect of Elohim and all the sons of the Most High eat of it, and whoever eats of it shall never die."
16.15: Then the divine messenger stretched out his right hand and took a small piece from the comb and ate, and with his own hand placed what was left in Asenath’s mouth and said to her, "Eat," and she ate.
16.16: And the messenger says to her: "See, now you have eaten the bread of life and have drunk the cup of immortality and been anointed with the ointment of incorruption; see, now today your flesh produces flowers of life from the fountain of the Most High, and your bones shall be made fat like the cedars of the Paradise of delight of Elohim, and unwearying powers shall maintain you; so your youth shall not see old age, nor shall your beauty ever fail, but you shall be like a walled mother-city of all."
16.17: And the messenger stirred the comb, and many bees arose from the cells of that comb, and the cells were numberless, tens of thousands of tens of thousands and thousands of thousands.
16.18: And the bees also were white like snow, and their wings like purple and crimson cloth and like scarlet; and they also had sharp stings and injured no man.
16.19: Then all those bees encircled Asenath from feet to head, and other great bees like their queens arose from the cells, and they circled around on her face and on her lips, and made a comb on her mouth and on her lips like the comb that lay before the messenger; and all those bees ate from the comb that was on Asenath’s mouth.
16.20: And the messenger said to the bees, "Go now to your place."
16.21: Then all the bees rose and flew and departed to the shamayim; but as many as wished to injure Asenath all fell to the earth and died.
16.22: And then the messenger stretched his staff over the dead bees and said to them: "Rise, and you also depart to your place."
16.23: Then all the dead bees rose and departed into the court that adjoined Asenath’s house and took up their lodging on the fruit-bearing trees.

17.1: And the messenger says to Asenath, "Have you seen this thing?"
17.2: And she said, "Yes, my master, I have seen all these things."
17.3: The divine messenger says to her: "So shall all my words be, as many as I have spoken to you today."
17.4: Then the messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 for the third time stretched out his right hand and touched the side of the comb, and immediately fire came up from the table and devoured the comb, but it did not injure the table at all.
17.5: And when much fragrance had come forth from the burning of the comb and filled the chamber, Asenath said to the divine messenger: "Master, I have seven virgins who were brought up with me from my youth and were born on one night with me, who wait on me, and I love them all as my sisters.
17.6: I will call them, and you shall baraḵ them too, just as you baraḵ me."
17.7: And the messenger said to her: "Call them."
17.8: Then Asenath called the seven virgins and set them before the messenger, and the messenger said to them: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim Most High shall baraḵ you, and you shall be … of refuge of seven cities, and all the elect of that city who dwell together shall … forever."
17.9: And after these things the divine messenger says to Asenath: "Take away this table."
17.10: And when Asenath turned to remove the table, immediately he departed from her eyes, and Asenath saw as it were a chariot with four horses that were going eastward to the shamayim, and the chariot was like a flame of fire, and the horses like lightning, and the messenger was standing above that chariot.
17.11: Then Asenath said: "Silly and foolish am I, the lowly one, for I have spoken as though a man came into my chamber from the shamayim, and I did not know that Elohim came into it; and see, now He is going back to the shamayim, to His place."
17.12: And she said within herself: "Be gracious, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to Your slave, and spare Your female servant, because, for my part, I have spoken rash things before You in ignorance."

18.1: And while Asenath was still speaking these words to herself, see, a young man, one of the servants of Yosĕph, saying: "Yosĕph, the mighty man of Elohim, is coming to you today."
18.2: And immediately Asenath called the overseer of her house and said to him: "Hurry and prepare my house and make a good dinner ready, for Yosĕph, the mighty man of Elohim, is coming to us today."
18.3: And the overseer of the house, when he saw her, sorrowed and wept; and he took hold of her right hand and kissed it tenderly and said: "What is wrong with you, my mistress, that your face is so shrunken?"
18.4: And she said: "I have had great pain in my head, and sleep departed from my eyes."
18.5: Then the overseer of the house went away and prepared the house and the dinner.
18.6: And Asenath remembered the messenger’s words and his instructions, and hurried and entered her second chamber, where the chests of her adornment were, and opened her great chest and brought out her first robe, like lightning to look at, and put it on; and she also girded herself with a bright and royal girdle that was of gold and precious stones, and on her hands she put golden bracelets, and on her feet golden boots, and a precious ornament about her neck, and she put a golden wreath about her head; and on the wreath, as on its front, was a great sapphire stone, and around the great stone six stones of great price, and with a very marvelous mantle she veiled her head.
18.7: And when Asenath remembered the words of the overseer of her house, because he had said to her that her face had shrunk, she sorrowed exceedingly, and groaned and said: "Woe is me, the lowly one, since my face is shrunken. Yosĕph will see me like this and I will be despised by him."
18.8: And she says to her female servant, "Bring me pure water from the fountain."
18.9: And when she had brought it, she poured it out into the basin, and bending down to wash her face, she sees her own face shining like the sun, and her eyes like the morning star when it rises, and her cheeks like a star of the shamayim, and her lips like red roses; the hairs of her head were like the vine that blooms among its fruits in the Paradise of Elohim, her neck like an all-variegated cypress.
18.10: And Asenath, when she saw these things, marveled within herself at the sight and rejoiced with exceedingly great joy and did not wash her face, for she said, "Lest I wash off this great and graceful beauty."
18.11: The overseer of her house then came back to tell her, "Everything you commanded is done"; and when he saw her, he feared greatly and was seized with trembling for a long time, and he fell at her feet and began to say: "What is this, my mistress? What is this beauty that surrounds you, that is great and marvelous? Has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of the shamayim chosen you as a bride for His son Yosĕph?"

19.1: And while they were still speaking these things, a boy came saying to Asenath: "See, Yosĕph is standing before the doors of our court."
19.2: Then Asenath hurried and went down the stairs from her loft with the seven virgins to meet Yosĕph and stood in the porch of her house.
19.3: And when Yosĕph had come into the court, the gates were shut and all strangers remained outside.
19.4: And Asenath came out from the porch to meet Yosĕph, and when he saw her he marveled at her beauty and said to her: "Who are you, young woman? Tell me quickly."
19.5: And she says to him: "I, master, am your female servant Asenath; all the idols I have cast away from me, and they perished.
19.6: And a man came to me today from the shamayim and has given me bread of life and I ate, and I drank a baruḵ cup, and he said to me: 'I have given you as a bride to Yosĕph, and he himself shall be your bridegroom forever; and your name shall not be called Asenath, but it shall be called "City of Refuge," and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim shall reign over many nations, and through you they shall seek refuge with Elohim Most High.'
19.7: And the man said: 'I will also go to Yosĕph, that I may speak into his ears these words concerning you.'
19.8: And now you know, master, whether that man has come to you and whether he has spoken to you concerning me."
19.9: Then Yosĕph says to Asenath: "Baruḵ are you, woman, of Elohim Most High, and baruḵ is your name forever, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim has laid the foundations of your walls, and the sons of the living Elohim shall dwell in your city of refuge, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim shall reign over them forever.
19.10: For that man came from the shamayim to me today and said these words to me concerning you.
19.11: And now come here to me, you virgin and pure; why do you stand far off?"
19.12: Then Yosĕph stretched out his hands and embraced Asenath, and Asenath Yosĕph, and they kissed one another for a long time, and both lived again in their spirit.
19.13: And Yosĕph kissed Asenath and gave her the spirit of life; then the second time he gave her the spirit of wisdom, and the third time he kissed her tenderly and gave her the spirit of truth.

2.1: But Asenath despised and scorned every man, being boastful and haughty, and no man had ever seen her, because Poti-Phera had a tower adjoining his house, exceedingly great and high, and above the tower was a loft containing ten chambers.
2.2: And the first chamber was great and very lovely and paved with purple stones, and its walls were faced with precious stones of many colors, and the roof of that chamber was also of gold.
2.3: And within that chamber the elohim of the Mitsrites, of which there was no number, gold and silver, were fixed, and Asenath worshipped all of them, and she feared them, and she performed sacrifices to them every day.
2.4: And the second chamber contained all Asenath’s adornments and chests, and there was gold in it, and much silver, and gold-woven clothing without limit, and choice stones of great price, and fine garments of linen, and all the adornment of her virginity was there.
2.5: And the third chamber was Asenath’s storehouse, containing all the good things of the earth.
2.6: And the remaining seven chambers were occupied by the seven virgins who served Asenath, each one having one chamber, for they were of the same age, born on the same night as Asenath, and she loved them very much; and they too were exceedingly beautiful, like the stars of the shamayim, and no man or male child ever spoke with them.
2.7: Now Asenath’s great chamber, where her virginity was fostered, had three windows; and the first window was very large, looking over the court to the east; and the second looked toward the south, and the third looked over the street.
2.8: And a golden bedstead stood in the chamber, facing east; and the bed was spread with purple cloth interwoven with gold, the bed being woven of scarlet and crimson cloth and fine linen.
2.9: On this bed Asenath slept alone, and no man or other woman had ever sat on it.
2.10: And there was also a great court adjoining the house all around, and an exceedingly high wall around the court, built of great rectangular stones; and there were also four gates in the court overlaid with iron, and each of these was guarded by eighteen strong, armed young men; and along the wall were also planted beautiful trees of every kind, all bearing fruit, their fruit being ripe, for it was the season of harvest; and there was also a rich spring of water flowing from the right side of the same court; and beneath the spring was a great cistern receiving the water of that spring, from which there flowed, as it were, a river through the middle of the court, and it watered all the trees of that court.

20.1: And when they had embraced one another for a long time and intertwined the chains of their hands, Asenath said to Yosĕph: "Come here, master, and enter our house, for on my part I have prepared our house and a great dinner."
20.2: And she took hold of his right hand and led him into her house and seated him on the chair of Poti-Phera her father; and she brought water to wash his feet.
20.3: And Yosĕph said: "Let one of the virgins come and wash my feet."
20.4: And Asenath said to him: "No, master, for from now on you are my master and I am your female servant. And why do you seek this, that another virgin should wash your feet? For your feet are my feet, and your hands my hands, and your soul my soul, and another shall not wash your feet."
20.5: And she urged him and washed his feet.
20.6: Then Yosĕph took hold of her right hand and kissed her tenderly, and Asenath kissed his head tenderly, and then he seated her at his right hand.
20.7: Her father and mother and all her relatives then came from the possession of their inheritance, and they saw her sitting with Yosĕph and clothed in a wedding garment.
20.8: And they marveled at her beauty and rejoiced and esteemed Elohim who gives life to the dead.
20.9: And after these things they ate and drank; and when all had made merry, Poti-Phera said to Yosĕph: "Tomorrow I will call all the princes and satraps of all the land of Mitsrayim, and will make a wedding for you, and you shall take my daughter Asenath as your wife."
20.10: But Yosĕph said: "I am going tomorrow to Pharaoh the meleḵ, for he himself is my father and appointed me ruler over all this land, and I will speak to him concerning Asenath, and he will give her to me as a wife."
20.11: And Poti-Phera said to him: "Go in peace."

21.1: And Yosĕph stayed that day with Poti-Phera, and he did not go in to Asenath, for he used to say: "It is not fitting for a man who worships Elohim to sleep with his wife before his marriage."
21.2: And Yosĕph rose early and departed to Pharaoh and said to him: "Give me Asenath, daughter of Poti-Phera, priest of On, as a wife."
21.3: And Pharaoh rejoiced with great joy, and he says to Yosĕph: "See, has not this one been betrothed to you as a wife from eternity? So let her be your wife from now on and to all eternity."
21.4: Then Pharaoh sent and called Poti-Phera, and Poti-Phera brought Asenath and set her before Pharaoh; and Pharaoh, when he saw her, marveled at her beauty and said: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yosĕph, shall baraḵ you, child, and this beauty of yours shall remain to eternity, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Elohim of Yosĕph, chose you as a bride for him; for Yosĕph is like the son of the Most High, and you shall be called his bride from now on and forever."
21.5: And after these things Pharaoh took Yosĕph and Asenath and set golden wreaths on their heads, which had been in his house from of old and from ancient times, and Pharaoh set Asenath at Yosĕph’s right hand.
21.6: And Pharaoh put his hands on their heads and said: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim Most High shall baraḵ you and shall multiply and magnify and esteem you to all eternity."
21.7: Then Pharaoh turned them around to face one another and brought them mouth to mouth, and they kissed one another.
21.8: And Pharaoh made a wedding for Yosĕph and a great dinner and much drinking during seven days, and he called together all the rulers of Mitsrayim and all the melaḵim of the nations, having made a proclamation in the land of Mitsrayim, saying: "Every man who does work during the seven days of the wedding of Yosĕph and Asenath shall surely die."
21.9: And while the wedding was going on, and when the dinner was ended, Yosĕph went in to Asenath, and Asenath conceived by Yosĕph and bore Menashsheh and Ephrayim his brother in Yosĕph’s house.

22.1: And when the seven years of plenty had passed, the seven years of famine began to come.
22.2: And when Ya’aqoḇ heard about Yosĕph his son, he came into Mitsrayim with all his relatives in the second year of the famine, in the second month, on the twenty-first of the month, and settled in Goshen.
22.3: And Asenath said to Yosĕph: "I will go and see your father, for your father Yisra’ĕl is like my father and Elohim."
22.4: And Yosĕph said to her: "You shall go with me and see my father."
22.5: And Yosĕph and Asenath came to Ya’aqoḇ in the land of Goshen, and Yosĕph’s brothers met them and bowed down to them with their faces to the earth.
22.6: Then both went in to Ya’aqoḇ; and Ya’aqoḇ was sitting on his bed, and he himself was an old man in a vigorous old age.
22.7: And when Asenath saw him, she marveled at his beauty, for Ya’aqoḇ was exceedingly beautiful to look at, and his old age like the youth of a graceful man, and all his head was white like snow, and the hairs of his head were all exceedingly close and thick, and his beard white, reaching to his breast, his eyes cheerful and gleaming, his sinews and his shoulders and his arms like those of a messenger, his thighs and his calves and his feet like those of a giant.
22.8: Then Asenath, when she saw him like this, marveled and fell down and bowed down on her face to the earth.
22.9: And Ya’aqoḇ said to Yosĕph: "Is this my daughter-in-law, your wife? She shall be baruḵ of Elohim Most High."
22.10: Then Ya’aqoḇ called Asenath to himself and baraḵ her and kissed her tenderly; and Asenath stretched out her hands and took hold of Ya’aqoḇ’s neck and hung on his neck and kissed him tenderly.
22.11: And after these things they ate and drank.
22.12: And then both Yosĕph and Asenath went to their house; and Shim’on and Lĕwi, the sons of Lĕ’ah, alone escorted them, but the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, the female servants of Lĕ’ah and Raḥĕl, did not join in escorting them, because they envied and detested them.
22.13: And Lĕwi was at Asenath’s right and Shim’on at her left.
22.14: And Asenath took hold of Lĕwi’s hand, because she loved him exceedingly, above all Yosĕph’s brothers, as a prophet and a worshipper of Elohim and one who feared 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
22.15: For he was a man of understanding and a prophet of the Most High, and he himself saw letters written in the shamayim and read them and revealed them to Asenath in secret; for Lĕwi himself also loved Asenath much and saw the place of her rest in the highest.

23.1: And it came to pass, as Yosĕph and Asenath were passing by when they were going to Ya’aqoḇ, that Pharaoh’s first-born son saw them from the wall, and when he saw Asenath, he became infatuated with her because of her surpassing beauty.
23.2: Then Pharaoh’s son sent messengers and called Shim’on and Lĕwi to him; and when they came and stood before him, Pharaoh’s first-born son says to them: "I for my part know that you are today mighty men above all men on the earth, and with these right hands of yours the city of the Sheḵemites was overthrown, and with your two swords 30,000 warriors were cut down.
23.3: And today I will take you to myself as companions and give you much gold and silver and male and female servants and houses and great inheritances; and fight on my side and do me a kindness, for I received a great outrage from your brother Yosĕph, since he himself took Asenath as a wife, and this woman was betrothed to me from of old.
23.4: And now come with me, and I will fight against Yosĕph to slay him with my sword, and I will take Asenath as a wife, and you shall be to me as brothers and faithful friends.
23.5: But if you will not listen to my words, I will slay you with my sword."
23.6: And when he had said these things, he drew out his sword and showed it to them.
23.7: And Shim’on was a bold and daring man, and he thought to lay his right hand on the hilt of his sword and draw it from its sheath and smite Pharaoh’s son, because he had spoken hard words to them.
23.8: Lĕwi then saw the thought of his heart, because he was a prophet, and trod with his foot on Shim’on’s right foot and pressed it, signaling to him to cease from his wrath.
23.9: And Lĕwi was saying quietly to Shim’on: "Why are you angry with this man? We are men who worship Elohim, and it is not fitting for us to repay evil for evil."
23.10: Then Lĕwi said to Pharaoh’s son openly, with mildness of heart: "Why does our master speak these words? We are men who worship Elohim, and our father is a friend of Elohim Most High, and our brother is like a son of Elohim.
23.11: And how shall we do this wicked thing, to sin in the sight of our Elohim and of our father Yisra’ĕl and in the sight of our brother Yosĕph?
23.12: And now hear my words. It is not fitting for a man who worships Elohim to injure any man in any way; and if anyone wishes to injure a man who worships Elohim, that man who worships Elohim does not avenge himself on him, because there is no sword in his hands.
23.13: And beware of speaking these words about our brother Yosĕph any more.
23.14: But if you continue in your evil counsel, see, our swords are drawn against you."
23.15: Then Shim’on and Lĕwi drew their swords from their sheaths and said: "Do you see these swords now? With these two swords 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 punished the outrage of the Sheḵemites, with which they outraged the sons of Yisra’ĕl through our sister Dinah, whom Sheḵem the son of Ḥamor defiled."
23.16: And Pharaoh’s son, when he saw the swords drawn, feared exceedingly and trembled over all his body, because they glittered like a flame of fire, and his eyes became dim, and he fell on his face on the earth beneath their feet.
23.17: Then Lĕwi stretched out his right hand and took hold of him, saying: "Stand up and do not fear; only beware of speaking any evil word concerning our brother Yosĕph any more."
23.18: And so both Shim’on and Lĕwi went out from before his face.

24.1: Pharaoh’s son then continued to be full of fear and grief, because he feared Yosĕph’s brothers, and again he was exceedingly infatuated because of Asenath’s beauty, and grieved greatly.
24.2: Then his servants say in his ear: "See, the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, the female servants of Lĕ’ah and Raḥĕl, Ya’aqoḇ’s wives, are at great enmity against Yosĕph and Asenath and hate them; these will be yours in all things, according to your will."
24.3: Immediately, therefore, Pharaoh’s son sent messengers and called them, and they came to him at the first hour of the night, and they stood in his presence, and he says to them: "I have learned from many that you are mighty men."
24.4: And Dan and Gaḏ, the older brothers, said to him: "Let my master now speak to his servants what he wishes, that your servants may hear and we may do according to your will."
24.5: Then Pharaoh’s son rejoiced with exceedingly great joy and said to his servants: "Withdraw from me now for a short while, for I have a secret conversation to hold with these men."
24.7: Then Pharaoh’s son lied, and he says to them: "See, now beraḵah and death are before your faces; so take the beraḵah rather than death, because you are mighty men and will not die like women; but be brave and avenge yourselves on your enemies.
24.8: For I have heard Yosĕph your brother saying to Pharaoh my father: 'Dan and Gaḏ and Naphtali and Ashĕr are not my brothers, but children of my father’s female servants; I am waiting, therefore, for my father’s death, and I will blot them out from the earth, and all their offspring, so that they do not inherit with us, because they are children of female servants.
24.9: For these also sold me to the Yishma’ĕlites, and I will repay them according to the outrage which they wickedly committed against me; only my father must die.'
24.10: And my father Pharaoh commended him for these things and said to him: 'You have spoken well, child. So take mighty men from me and proceed against them according to what they did against you, and I will be a helper to you.'"
24.11: And when Dan and Gaḏ heard these things from Pharaoh’s son, they were much troubled and grieved exceedingly, and they said to him: "We beg you, master, help us; for from now on we are your slaves and servants and will die with you."
24.12: And Pharaoh’s son said: "I will be a helper to you if you also will listen to my words."
24.13: And they said to him: "Command us what you wish, and we will do according to your will."
24.14: And Pharaoh’s son says to them: "I will slay my father Pharaoh this night, because Pharaoh is like Yosĕph’s father and said to him that he would help against you; and you slay Yosĕph, and I will take Asenath to myself as a wife, and you shall be my brothers and fellow-heirs of all my possessions. Only do this thing."
24.15: And Dan and Gaḏ said to him: "We are your servants today and will do all things that you have commanded us. And we have heard Yosĕph saying to Asenath: 'Go tomorrow to the possession of our inheritance, for it is the season of the vintage'; and he sent six hundred men mighty in war with her, and fifty forerunners. Now therefore hear us, and we will speak to our master."
24.16: And they spoke to him all their secret words.
24.17: Then Pharaoh’s son gave the four brothers five hundred men each and appointed them their chiefs and leaders.
24.18: And Dan and Gaḏ said to him: "We are your servants today and will do all the things that you have commanded us, and we will set out by night and lie in wait in the ravine and hide ourselves in the thicket of the reeds; and you take fifty bowmen on horses with you and go a long way ahead of us, and Asenath will come and fall into our hands, and we will cut down the men who are with her, and she herself will flee ahead with her chariot and fall into your hands, and you shall do to her as your soul desires; and after these things we will slay Yosĕph also while he is grieving for Asenath; likewise we will also slay his children before his eyes."
24.19: Pharaoh’s first-born son then, when he heard these things, rejoiced exceedingly, and he sent them out, and two thousand fighting men with them.
24.20: And when they came to the ravine, they hid themselves in the thicket of the reeds, and they divided into four companies, and took up their position on the far side of the ravine as in the front part, five hundred men on this side of the road and on that; and on the near side of the ravine the rest likewise remained, and they themselves also took up their position in the thicket of the reeds, five hundred men on this side and on that of the road; and between them was a broad and wide road.

25.1: Then Pharaoh’s son rose up the same night and came to his father’s bedchamber to slay him with the sword.
25.2: His father’s guards then hindered him from coming in to his father and said to him: "What do you command, master?"
25.3: And Pharaoh’s son said to them: "I wish to see my father, for I am going to gather the vintage of my newly planted vineyard."
25.4: And the guards said to him: "Your father is in pain and lay awake the whole night and is now resting, and he said to us that no one was to come in to him, 'not even if it is my first-born son.'"
25.5: And on hearing these things he went away in wrath and immediately took mounted bowmen, fifty in number, and went away ahead of them, as Dan and Gaḏ had said to him.
25.6: And the younger brothers Naphtali and Ashĕr spoke to their older brothers Dan and Gaḏ, saying: "Why do you, for your part, again work wickedness against your father Yisra’ĕl and against your brother Yosĕph?
25.7: And Elohim preserves him as the apple of an eye.
25.8: See, did you not once sell Yosĕph? And he is meleḵ today of all the land of Mitsrayim and food-giver.
25.9: Now therefore, if you again wish to work wickedness against him, he will cry to the Most High, and He will send fire from the shamayim and it will devour you, and the messengers of Elohim will fight against you."
25.10: Then the older brothers were moved to anger against them and said: "And shall we die like women? Far be it."
25.11: And they went out to meet Yosĕph and Asenath.

26.1: And Asenath rose in the morning and said to Yosĕph: "I am going to the possession of our inheritance as you have said; but my soul is exceedingly afraid, because you are parting from me."
26.2: And Yosĕph said to her: "Take courage and do not be afraid, but rather go away rejoicing, in dread of no man whatsoever, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with you, and He Himself will preserve you as the apple of an eye from every evil.
26.3: And I will set out to distribute food and will give to all the men in the city, and no man shall perish of hunger in the land of Mitsrayim."
26.4: Then Asenath departed on her way, and Yosĕph to distribute food.
26.5: And when Asenath reached the place of the ravine with the six hundred men, suddenly those who were with Pharaoh’s son came out from their ambush and joined battle with those who were with Asenath, and cut them all down with their swords, and they slew all her forerunners, but Asenath fled with her chariot.
26.6: Then Lĕwi, the son of Lĕ’ah, knew all these things by the Ruaḥ as a prophet and told his brothers of Asenath’s danger, and immediately each of them took his sword on his thigh and their shields on their arms and the spears in their right hands, and pursued after Asenath with great speed.
26.7: And as Asenath was fleeing ahead, see, Pharaoh’s son met her, and fifty horsemen with him; and Asenath, when she saw him, was seized with very great fear and was trembling, and she called on the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 her Elohim.

27.1: And Binyamin was sitting with her on the chariot on the right side; and Binyamin was a strong lad of about nineteen years, and on him was ineffable beauty and might like that of a lion’s cub, and he was also one who feared Elohim exceedingly.
27.2: Then Binyamin leaped down from the chariot and took a round stone from the ravine and filled his hand, and hurled it at Pharaoh’s son and smote his left temple, and wounded him with a grievous wound, and he fell from his horse to the earth half-dead.
27.3: And then Binyamin, having run up onto a rock, says to Asenath’s charioteer: "Give me stones from the ravine."
27.4: And he gave him fifty stones.
27.5: And Binyamin hurled the stones and slew the fifty men who were with Pharaoh’s son, all the stones sinking in through their temples.
27.6: Then the sons of Lĕ’ah, Re’uḇĕn and Shim’on, Lĕwi and Yahuḏah, Yissasḵar and Zeḇulun, pursued after the men who had lain in wait against Asenath and fell upon them unawares and cut them all down; and the six men slew two thousand and seventy-six men.
27.7: And the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah fled from their face and said: "We have perished at the hands of our brothers, and Pharaoh’s son has also died by the hand of Binyamin the lad, and all who were with him perished by the hand of the boy Binyamin.
27.8: So then, come, let us slay Asenath and Binyamin and flee to the thicket of these reeds."
27.9: And they came against Asenath, holding their swords drawn, covered with blood.
27.10: And Asenath, when she saw them, feared greatly and said: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, who gave me life and delivered me from the idols and the corruption of death, just as You said to me that my soul shall live forever, deliver me now also from these wicked men."
27.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim heard Asenath’s voice, and immediately the swords of the adversaries fell from their hands to the earth and were turned into ashes.

28.1: And the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, when they saw the strange miracle that had been done, feared and said: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is fighting against us on Asenath’s behalf."
28.2: Then they fell on their faces on the earth and bowed down to Asenath and said: "Have mercy on us, your servants, for you are our mistress and queen.
28.3: We wickedly committed evil deeds against you and against our brother Yosĕph, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 repaid us according to our works.
28.4: Therefore we, your servants, beg you, have mercy on us, the lowly and miserable, and deliver us from the hands of our brothers, for they will make themselves avengers of the outrage done to you, and their swords are against us.
28.5: So be gracious to your servants, mistress, before them."
28.6: And Asenath said to them: "Take courage and do not be afraid of your brothers, for they themselves are men who worship Elohim and fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; but go into the thicket of these reeds until I appease them on your behalf and stay their wrath on account of the great crimes which you, for your part, have dared to commit against them.
28.7: But may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 see and judge between me and you."
28.8: Then Dan and Gaḏ fled into the thicket of the reeds; and their brothers, Lĕ’ah’s sons, came running like stags with great speed against them.
28.9: And Asenath stepped down from the chariot that was her shelter and gave them her right hand with tears, and they themselves fell down and bowed down to her on the earth and wept with a loud voice; and they kept asking for their brothers, the sons of the female servants, in order to put them to death.
28.10: And Asenath said to them: "I beg you, spare your brothers, and do not repay them evil for evil.
28.11: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saved me from them and shattered their daggers and swords out of their hands, and see, they have melted and were burned to ashes on the earth like wax before fire, and this is sufficient for us, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 fights for us against them.
28.12: So spare your brothers, for they are your brothers and the blood of your father Yisra’ĕl."
28.13: And Shim’on said to her: "Why does our mistress speak good words on behalf of her enemies? No, but rather we will cut them down limb from limb with our swords, because they devised evil things concerning our brother Yosĕph and our father Yisra’ĕl, and against you, our mistress, today."
28.14: Then Asenath stretched out her right hand and touched Shim’on’s beard and kissed him tenderly and said: "By no means, brother, repay evil for evil to your neighbor, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 will avenge this outrage.
28.15: They themselves, you know, are your brothers and the offspring of your father Yisra’ĕl, and they fled far from your face.
28.17: Then Lĕwi came up to her and kissed her right hand tenderly, for he knew that she was eager to save the men from their brothers’ anger, so that they would not slay them.
28.18: And they themselves were near at hand in the thicket of the reed-bed; and Lĕwi his brother, knowing this, did not declare it to his brothers, for he feared that in their anger they would cut their brothers down.

29.1: And Pharaoh’s son rose from the earth and sat up and spat blood from his mouth, for the blood was running down from his temple into his mouth.
29.2: And Binyamin ran up to him and took his sword and drew it from Pharaoh’s son’s sheath and wished to smite Pharaoh’s son on the breast.
29.3: Then Lĕwi ran up to him and took hold of his hand and said: "By no means, brother, do this thing, for we are men who worship Elohim, and it is not fitting for a man who worships Elohim to repay evil for evil, nor to trample on one who has fallen, nor to crush his enemy utterly, even to death.
29.4: And now put the sword back in its place, and come and help me, and let us heal him of this wound; and if he lives, he will be our friend, and his father Pharaoh will be our father."
29.5: Then Lĕwi raised Pharaoh’s son from the earth and washed away the blood from his face and tied a bandage over his wound and set him on his horse and led him to his father Pharaoh, relating to him all the things that had happened and taken place.
29.6: And Pharaoh arose from his throne and bowed down to Lĕwi on the earth and baraḵ him.
29.7: Then, when the third day had passed, Pharaoh’s son died from the stone with which he was wounded by Binyamin.
29.8: And Pharaoh mourned for his first-born son exceedingly, so that from the grief Pharaoh fell sick and died at 109 years, and he left his diadem to the all-beautiful Yosĕph.
29.9: And Yosĕph reigned alone in Mitsrayim 48 years; and after these things Yosĕph gave back the diadem to Pharaoh’s younger child, who was at the breast when the old man Pharaoh died.
29.10: And Yosĕph was from then on like a father of Pharaoh’s younger child in Mitsrayim until his death, esteeming and praising Elohim.

3.1: And it came to be in the first year of the seven years of plenty, in the fourth month, on the twenty-eighth of the month, that Yosĕph came to the borders of On, collecting the grain of that district.
3.2: And when Yosĕph drew near to that city, he sent twelve men ahead of him to Poti-Phera, the priest of On, saying: "I will come in to you today, because it is the time of noon and of the midday meal, and the heat of the sun is great, and so that I may cool myself under the roof of your house."
3.3: And Poti-Phera, when he heard these things, rejoiced with exceedingly great joy, and said: "Baruḵ be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yosĕph, because my master Yosĕph has thought me worthy."
3.4: And Poti-Phera called the overseer of his house and said to him: "Hurry and make my house ready, and prepare a great dinner, because Yosĕph, the mighty one of Elohim, is coming to us today."
3.5: And when Asenath heard that her father and mother had come from the possession of their inheritance, she rejoiced greatly and said: "I will go and see my father and mother, because they have come from the possession of our inheritance."
3.6: And Asenath hurried into her chamber where her robes lay and put on a fine linen robe made of crimson cloth and interwoven with gold, and girded herself with a golden girdle, and put bracelets around her hands; and on her feet she put golden boots, and around her neck she placed an ornament of great price and precious stones, which were embellished on all sides, having the names of the elohim of the Mitsrites engraved everywhere on them, both on the bracelets and on the stones; and she also put a tiara on her head and bound a diadem around her temples and covered her head with a mantle.

4.1: And then she hurried and went down the stairs from her loft and came to her father and mother and kissed them.
4.2: And Poti-Phera and his wife rejoiced over their daughter Asenath with exceedingly great joy, for they saw her adorned and embellished like a bride of Elohim; and they brought out all the good things which they had brought from the possession of their inheritance and gave them to their daughter; and Asenath rejoiced over all the good things, over the late summer fruit and the grapes and the dates and the doves, and over the mulberries and the figs, because they were all fine and pleasant to the taste.
4.3: And Poti-Phera said to his daughter Asenath: "Child." And she said: "Here I am, my master."
4.4: And he said to her: "Sit down between us, and I will speak my words to you."
4.5: And she sat down between her father and her mother, and Poti-Phera her father took hold of her right hand with his right hand and kissed it tenderly and said: "Dearest child." And she said to him: "Here I am, my master father."
4.6: And Poti-Phera said to her: "See, Yosĕph, the mighty one of Elohim, is coming to us today, and this man is ruler of all the land of Mitsrayim; and Meleḵ Pharaoh appointed him ruler of all our land and meleḵ, and he himself gives grain to all this country and saves it from the coming famine; and this Yosĕph is a man who worships Elohim, and is discreet, and a virgin as you are today, and a man mighty in wisdom and knowledge, and the Ruaḥ of Elohim is upon him and the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is in him.
4.7: Come, dearest child, and I will give you to him as a wife, and you shall be his bride, and he himself shall be your bridegroom forever."
4.8: And when Asenath heard these words from her father, a great sweat poured out over her face, and she became furious with great anger, and she looked askance at her father with her eyes and said: "Why, my master father, do you speak these words?
4.9: Do you wish to give me over as a captive to a foreigner, a fugitive, and one who has been sold?
4.10: Is this not the son of the shepherd from the land of Kena’an? And he himself has been left behind by him.
4.11: Is this not he who lay with his mistress, and his master threw him into the prison of darkness, and Pharaoh brought him out of the prison because he interpreted his dream, just as the older women of the Mitsrites also interpret?
4.12: No, but I will be married to the meleḵ’s first-born son, because he himself is meleḵ of all the land."
4.13: When he heard these things, Poti-Phera was ashamed to speak further to his daughter Asenath about Yosĕph, because she answered him with boastfulness and anger.

5.1: And see, a young man of Poti-Phera’s servants rushed in, and he says to him: "See, Yosĕph is standing before the doors of our court."
5.2: And when Asenath heard these words she fled from the face of her father and mother and went up into the loft, and she came into her chamber and stood at the great window looking east to see Yosĕph coming into her father’s house.
5.3: And Poti-Phera came out, with his wife and all their relatives and their servants, to meet Yosĕph; and when the gates of the court that faced east were opened, Yosĕph came in seated in the second chariot of Pharaoh; and four horses, white as snow, with golden bits, were yoked to it, and the chariot was made entirely of pure gold.
5.4: And Yosĕph was clothed in a white and rare tunic, and the robe that was thrown around him was purple, made of fine linen interwoven with gold, and a golden wreath was upon his head, and around his wreath were twelve choice stones, and above the stones twelve golden rays, and in his right hand a royal staff, which had an olive branch stretched out, and there was an abundance of fruit on it.
5.5: When, then, Yosĕph had come into the court and its doors had been shut, and every stranger, man and woman, remained outside the court, for the guards of the gates pulled the doors to and closed them, Poti-Phera came with his wife and all their relatives except their daughter Asenath, and they bowed down to Yosĕph with their faces to the earth; and Yosĕph got down from his chariot and greeted them with his hand.

6.1: And when Asenath saw Yosĕph she was deeply stung in her soul and her heart was crushed, and her knees went weak and her whole body trembled and she feared with great fear, and then she groaned and said in her heart: "Alas, miserable me! Where now shall I, the wretched one, go away?
6.2: Or where shall I be hidden from his face?
6.3: Or how shall Yosĕph the son of Elohim see me, since I, for my part, have spoken evil things about him?
6.4: Alas, miserable me! Where shall I go away and be hidden, because he himself sees every hiding place, and knows all things, and no hidden thing escapes him because of the great light that is in him?
6.5: And now may the Elohim of Yosĕph be gracious to me, because in ignorance I have spoken wicked words against him. What now shall I, the wretched one, follow?
6.6: Have I not said: 'Yosĕph is coming, the son of the shepherd from the land of Kena’an'?
6.7: Now therefore he has come to us in his chariot like the sun from the shamayim, and he entered our house today, and he shines into it like light upon the earth.
6.8: But I am foolish and bold, because I scorned him and spoke evil words about him and did not know that Yosĕph is a son of Elohim.
6.9: For who among men will ever beget such beauty, or what womb of woman will give birth to such light?
6.10: Wretched am I and foolish, because I have spoken evil words to my father.
6.11: Now, therefore, let my father give me to Yosĕph rather as a female servant and a slave, and I will be in bondage to him forever."

7.1: And Yosĕph came into the house of Poti-Phera and sat upon a chair.
7.2: And they washed his feet, and set a table before him separately, because Yosĕph did not eat with the Mitsrites, since this was an abomination to him.
7.3: And Yosĕph looked up and saw Asenath peeping out, and he says to Poti-Phera: "Who is that woman who is standing in the loft by the window? Let her go away from this house."
7.4: For Yosĕph was afraid, saying: "Perhaps she too will annoy me."
7.5: For all the wives and daughters of the princes and the satraps of all the land of Mitsrayim used to annoy him in order that they might lie with him; and many wives and daughters of the Mitsrites also, as many as saw Yosĕph, were distressed on account of his beauty; and the envoys whom the women sent to him with gold and silver and precious gifts Yosĕph sent back with threats and insults, saying: "I will not sin in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim and before the face of my father Yisra’ĕl."
7.6: For Yosĕph always had Elohim before his eyes and always remembered the instructions of his father; for Ya’aqoḇ often spoke to and admonished his son Yosĕph and all his sons: "Guard yourselves securely, children, from a strange woman, so as not to have fellowship with her, for fellowship with her is ruin and destruction."
7.7: Therefore Yosĕph said: "Let that woman depart from this house."
7.8: And Poti-Phera said to him: "My master, that woman whom you have seen standing in the loft is not a stranger, but is our daughter, one who hates every man, and no other man has ever seen her except you alone today; and if you wish, master, she shall come and speak to you, for our daughter is like your sister."
7.9: And Yosĕph rejoiced with exceedingly great joy, because Poti-Phera said: "She is a virgin who hates every man."
7.10: And Yosĕph said to Poti-Phera and his wife: "If she is your daughter, and is a virgin, let her come, for she is my sister, and from today I love her as my sister."

8.1: Then her mother went up into the loft and brought Asenath to Yosĕph, and Poti-Phera said to her: "Kiss your brother, because he also is a virgin, just as you are today, and he hates every strange woman, just as you hate every strange man."
8.2: And Asenath said to Yosĕph: "Greetings, master, baruḵ of Elohim Most High."
8.3: And Yosĕph said to her: "Elohim, who gives life to all things, shall baraḵ you, young woman."
8.4: Poti-Phera then says to his daughter Asenath: "Come and kiss your brother."
8.5: When Asenath then came up to kiss Yosĕph, Yosĕph stretched out his right hand and laid it on her chest between her two breasts, and Yosĕph said: "It is not fitting for a man who worships Elohim, who baraḵ the living Elohim with his mouth, and eats the baruḵ bread of life, and drinks the baruḵ cup of immortality, and is anointed with the baruḵ ointment of incorruption, to kiss a strange woman, who baraḵ dead and deaf idols with her mouth, and eats from their table the bread of strangling, and drinks from their libation the cup of deceit, and is anointed with the ointment of destruction; but the man who worships Elohim will kiss his mother, and the sister who is born of his mother, and the sister who is born of his tribe, and the wife who shares his couch, who baraḵ the living Elohim with their mouth."
8.6: "Likewise it is also not fitting for a woman who worships Elohim to kiss a strange man, for this is an abomination in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim."
8.7: And when Asenath heard these words from Yosĕph, she was deeply distressed and groaned; and as she was looking steadily at Yosĕph with her eyes open, they were filled with tears.
8.8: And Yosĕph, when he saw her weeping, pitied her exceedingly, for he was mild and merciful and one who feared 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
8.9: Then he lifted up his right hand above her head and said: "𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of my father Yisra’ĕl, the Most High and the mighty Elohim, who gave life to all things and called from the darkness to the light and from error to truth and from death to life, baraḵ this virgin also, and give her life, and renew her with Your Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, and let her eat the bread of Your life and drink the cup of Your beraḵah, and number her with Your people whom You chose before all things were made, and let her enter into Your rest which You prepared for Your elect, and let her live in Your eternal life forever."

9.1: And Asenath rejoiced over the beraḵah of Yosĕph with exceedingly great joy.
9.2: Then she hurried and went up into her loft by herself, and fell upon her bed in weakness, for there was in her joy and sorrow and great fear; and a continuous sweat poured over her when she heard these words from Yosĕph, and when he spoke to her in the name of Elohim Most High.
9.3: Then she wept with great and bitter weeping, and she turned in penitence from her elohim whom she used to worship, and the idols, which she spurned, and waited for evening to come.
9.4: But Yosĕph ate and drank; and he told his servants to yoke the horses to their chariots, and to go around all the land.
9.5: And Poti-Phera said to Yosĕph: "Let my master lodge here today, and in the morning you shall go your way."
9.6: And Yosĕph said: "No, but I will go away today, for this is the day on which Elohim began to make all His created things, and on the eighth day I will also return to you and will lodge here."
